samples.text: Spiritual masters from across the Buddhist world are already building monasteries, retreat centers, libraries, and institutions of learning. So imagine what will exist side by side. Entrepreneurs and monks. Artificial intelligence and human consciousness. Data centers and meditation centers. The newest technology humanity has created alongside some of the world's oldest traditions for understanding the human mind. Is that a contradiction? No. In fact, that is the point. GMC is not asking investors to choose between commercial success and quality of life. It is designed for both. Because the world's best people choose more than a workplace. They choose where to build their lives. Taken together, these advantages create the conditions for businesses to grow and investors to prosper. Lower uncertainty, abundant clean energy, access to growth, the ability to attract global talent and the freedom to create the markets others will later enter. That is how GMC turns its values into commercial advantage. Now you may reasonably ask, it sounds wonderful, but is it real? Yes, it is real. The Royal Charter is in force. Laws have been enacted. Regulators are operating. The framework for an independent judiciary is in place. GMC has its own government, its own laws, its own financial systems, and its own gold-backed digital currency. These are not aspirations. They are foundations already in place. The physical city is also taking shape. Infrastructure is being built progressively as and when it is needed. The international airport is under construction. A railway connection to India's vast rail network is being developed. Energy, digital connectivity, and urban infrastructure are being added as demand grows. Artificial intelligence and data center projects are moving forward, and nearly $5 billion in projects are under active negotiation. GMC is not an idea waiting to begin. The journey has begun. But there is still an extraordinary opportunity to help define where it goes. And perhaps the best way to understand GMC is to imagine it as a startup. a 4,000 square kilometre start-up. Now, most start-ups begin with an idea, then search for the conditions they need to succeed.

Our people have embraced GMC as a people's project, an investment in our children, our economy, and our shared future. Bhutan is not waiting to see whether the world believes in GMC before committing to it. We have committed, fully. Now let me tell you why GMC is built to succeed. Begin with location. GMC sits directly on the border with India, our closest friend and neighbor. The vision enjoys the support of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the government of India, and our neighbors across the border in Assam. Beyond that border lies the world's most populous country and one of its largest and fastest growing economies. GMC is also a gateway to the markets of South Asia and Southeast Asia. So GMC begins with what many new cities spent decades trying to acquire. Access to vast and growing markets, connectivity, and in India, a trusted friend. Bhutan brings another advantage, one that cannot be bought. Trust. Trust built through peace, political stability, the rule of law, and a record for honoring our commitments. For long-term investors, trust creates something invaluable. Predictability. Bhutan has spent generations building that trust. GMC puts it to work. Then there is nature. Imagine GMC in the morning. Mist rising from its rivers. forest stretching towards the mountains, elephants moving through the landscape, tigers still roaming its forest. This is not empty land. It is a living, carbon-negative landscape, a biodiversity hotspot. We will not build over it. We will build within it and protect it. The forests, rivers, and wildlife of GMC are not obstacles to development. They are part of its value. And then there's energy. Bhutan is expanding its renewable energy capacity towards 25 gigawatts by 2040. That electricity will power GMC and the industries of the future. advanced manufacturing, scientific research, artificial intelligence and data centers, clean renewable power. But GMC has another type of power, a power Bhutan has cultivated for centuries, spiritual power. GMC is being developed as a global center for Vajrayana Buddhism.

Mr. President, Excellencies, Ladies and Gentlemen, I stand before you today not as a Prime Minister, but as a salesman. And I am here not to sell you a product, or a policy, or yet another declaration. I am here to sell you An idea. An idea conceived and spearheaded by His Majesty King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck. An idea embraced by the people of Bhutan. An idea already being built. That idea is Gyalpo Mindfulness City. And my sales pitch is simple. Come and build it with us. Now, the world has built new cities before. Financial centers, free ports, technology hubs, special economic zones. But GMC is different. You see, Gailipoo Mindfulness City is a special administrative region, an SAR. Under its royal charter, GMC exercises full autonomy in governance, legislation, and the judiciary. Think one country, two systems. Think of the agility of a microstate. But GMC was not inherited from history. It was not created to manage a transfer of sovereignty. It is being deliberately created by Bhutan, within Bhutan, on sovereign Bhutanese territory for the future. GMC covers more than 4,000 square kilometers. That is more than five times the size of Singapore. But its greatest opportunity is not its size. Its greatest opportunity is an institutional blank slate. GMC was given something extraordinarily rare, the freedom to design an entire city and its operating systems from first principles. So we asked, If you could begin again, how would you govern? What laws would you write? How would we regulate business? How would we guarantee an independent judiciary? How would we attract the best talent? How would we use technology and especially artificial intelligence? How would we create wealth while protecting nature? And ultimately, what would all that prosperity before. These were not theoretical questions. We answered them. And we are making full use of that institutional blank slate. If Singapore has legal principles that work, we learn from Singapore. If Abu Dhabi has financial regulations that work, we learn from Abu Dhabi.

Do not invent quotes, countries, numbers or mandates. Distinguish prepared text from delivered text, AI from generic digitalization, and uncertainty from No. Return the strict requested JSON. This is an automated review, never a claim of human verification. Read every representative and boundary passage. Propose analytical theme definitions grounded in these statements. Separate technical AI safety from military/security concerns when warranted. Include minority positions; do not force one theme per cluster or a predetermined number.
